prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 3 "Shipping": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 4 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 4 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 6 of 12 earlier cases, t = 0 in 6; when indemnified t per pc about 78 (80% range 68 to 88); revealed per pc: 12.9-16.1 (case 14), >=60 (case 16), >=68 (case 18), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21)
- line 9 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 6 of 12 earlier cases, t = 0 in 6; when indemnified t per pc about 78 (80% range 68 to 88); revealed per pc: 12.9-16.1 (case 14), >=60 (case 16), >=68 (case 18), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21)

items.rationale: The bicycle and its frame are excluded means of transport under 4.3(b); 7.1.8(a) excludes the replacement cost despite the insured break-in.
Clause 4.3(b) expressly excludes bicycle braking assemblies, and 7.1.8(a) excludes the cost of replacing them.
Carriage of the excluded bicycle is barred by 7.1.8(a); separately billed inbound shipping is also excluded under 7.1.8(d).
The vehicle charge serves only excluded bicycle work. Clauses 7.1.8(a) and (f) bar attendance where no work on that invoice is covered.
Clause 7.1.8(a) excludes assembly of the bicycle and its replacement parts because the bicycle is outside Part 4.
Under 7.1.8(a) and 7.1.10, these sundries follow the excluded bicycle work they served.
Clause 7.1.8(a) excludes labour of every grade on the bicycle, including the single apprentice hour.
All three skilled hours are allocated to the excluded bicycle repair under 7.1.8(a) and 7.1.10.
Clause 7.1.7(g) covers one attendance by the locksmith to secure the damaged back door. The gross allowance is €78 for that visit.

Fitting and adjusting the replacement lock are covered under 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d), at the pre-loss standard under 7.1.9. Allow €50 for the fitting charge, excluding any labour already billed separately under 7.1.8(g).
Clause 7.1.7(f) covers fixings and sundries incorporated into the damaged door or lock repair. Allow €20 for ordinary materials, not tools or administrative charges under 7.1.8(e).
Clause 7.1.7(e) expressly covers necessary apprentice labour on the insured repair. One hour at €40 gross gives a €40 allowance.
Clause 7.1.7(e) covers necessary skilled labour to restore the damaged lock and entry point. One hour at €95 gross gives a €95 allowance.
